title: the DDG front matter
include_after: #include "rules/ffq.h"  // R848: the FF magic item tables
audit_anchor: #include "rules/audits/r848_batch.h"  // R848: R848 FF magic item tables audit
audit_comment: THE DDG FRONT MATTER - the D&DG arc opener, print pp. 1-11: the title page, foreword, contents, preface, credits, the explanatory notes with the seven over-18 ability grids and the psionic class table, the standard divine abilities, the DMing doctrine with the intervention modifiers, the clerics and spell-granting ladder, the omens, the soul/spirit mortality doctrine, and the divine ascension requirements. Zero registry defs touched; the floor holds at 995. The physical-copy eyeball adjudications: the strength 23 damage +11 and the psionic class V lettered modes.

banner.title: the DDG front matter - the arc opener. DEITIES & DEMIGODS, the 1980 second printing (Ward with Kuntz), print pp. 1-11: the front matter walk.
banner.provenance: primary ink: the extract/ddg tesseract pass (commit cd645b4, pNNN_full.txt + pNNN_tsv.tsv, print = pdf - 1); the physical-copy eyeball settled the strength 23 damage +11, the psionic roman numerals I-VI and the class V lettered mode lists (A,B,C,E attack, F,G,H defense); the archive.org L&L parity voice is lending-gated and was not obtainable.
banner.sentinel: the odPd 0 sentinel encodes the single-number open-doors parentheses (five rows); the wisdom loLvl/loCnt 0 pair encodes the two-spell rows (23, 24); the constitution regen 0 is the Nil row; the psionic class VI row is all 0 with the asterisked invulnerability noted in the bools.

consts.name: dgaPantheonLeadersHp
consts.comment: all the leaders of the pantheons were given 400 hit points, the rest scaled down from there (the preface)

consts.name: dgaFreqVeryRare

consts.name: dgaFreqRare

consts.name: dgaFreqUncommon

consts.name: dgaFreqCommon

consts.name: dgaMrCasterBase
consts.comment: magic resistance is based on the spell being cast by an 11th level spell-caster

consts.name: dgaMrPerLevel
consts.comment: magic resistance adjusts 5% per level above or below the 11th level base

consts.name: dgaLevelFloorDemi
consts.comment: the magic ability and psionic discipline level floor for demigods (15th)

consts.name: dgaLevelFloorLesser
consts.comment: the level floor for lesser gods (20th)

consts.name: dgaLevelFloorGreater
consts.comment: the level floor for greater gods (25th)

consts.name: dgaStdAbilities
consts.comment: the eight standard divine abilities (command, comprehend languages, detect alignment, gate, geas, quest, teleport, true seeing)

consts.name: dgaCommandLesser
consts.comment: the command ability lasts 2 rounds for lesser gods

consts.name: dgaCommandGreater
consts.comment: the command ability lasts 3 rounds for greater gods

consts.name: dgaGeasRange
consts.comment: the geas ability: as the spell, but with a range of 9

consts.name: dgaQuestRange
consts.comment: the quest ability: as the spell with a range of 9 inches, and no saving throw

consts.name: dgaInterventionBase
consts.comment: the straight 10% chance some creature is sent if the beseeching character is exemplary and this is the first request

consts.name: dgaGodSave
consts.comment: all gods and demigods have a saving throw of 2 in all categories (only a 1 on d20 misses)

consts.name: dgaHeroSave
consts.comment: all heroes delineated in the book have saves of 3 in all categories

consts.name: dgaDivineRanks
consts.comment: the three divine ranks: demigod, lesser god, greater god

consts.name: dgaDemigodMaxSpell
consts.comment: a demigod cannot grant spells above 5th level

consts.name: dgaSoulRaces
consts.comment: the five soul races (humans, dwarves, halflings, gnomes, half-elves - the raise dead and resurrection targets)

consts.name: dgaDeathLagMin
consts.comment: the death-to-plane journey takes as little as 3 days relative to the Prime Material Plane

consts.name: dgaDeathLagMax
consts.comment: the death-to-plane journey takes up to 30 days relative to the Prime Material Plane

consts.name: dgaSpiritRestMin
consts.comment: a spirit may spend as little as ten years on its plane before returning to the Prime Material Plane

consts.name: dgaSpiritRestMax
consts.comment: a spirit may spend a millennium or more on its plane before returning (time is not important to a deity)

consts.name: dgaRestDemonsCentury
consts.comment: type V and VI demons must rest a century before returning unaided to the plane where they were slain

consts.name: dgaRestPrincesMin
consts.comment: demon princes and lords, greater devils and arch-devils require 2-8 weeks of rest

consts.name: dgaRestPrincesMax
consts.comment: the top of the 2-8 week demon prince rest range

consts.name: dgaRestGreaterMin
consts.comment: even greater deities require 1-4 weeks of rest before dealing with activities outside their home plane

consts.name: dgaRestGreaterMax
consts.comment: the top of the 1-4 week greater deity rest range

consts.name: dgaAscensionReqts
consts.comment: the four divine ascension requirements (level, abilities, worshipers, faithful follower)

consts.name: dgaAscAvg5Min
consts.comment: at an average campaign level of 5, an ascension candidate should be around 9th-10th level

consts.name: dgaAscAvg5Max
consts.comment: the top of the average-5 example (9th-10th level)

consts.name: dgaAscAvg15Min
consts.comment: at an average campaign level of 15, a candidate would be in the realm of 25th-30th level

consts.name: dgaAscAvg15Max
consts.comment: the top of the average-15 example (25th-30th level)

consts.name: dgaWishAgingYears
consts.comment: each wish spell weakens the caster and ages him or her 3 years (the ascension cost note)

consts.name: dgaOmenWispDays
consts.comment: the coming of a will-o-wisp means some building will burn to the ground within seven days

consts.name: dgaPsiClasses
consts.comment: the gods psionic abilities fall into six standardized classes (I-VI)

bools.name: dgaNotSupplement
bools.comment: the foreword thesis: do not fall into the error of regarding it as a supplement - it is integral to Dungeon Mastering a true AD&D campaign

bools.name: dgaForewordPantheonSelection
bools.comment: deities are presented in pantheons; the DM selects which ones, combinations, or parts of pantheons suit the campaign

bools.name: dgaDemigodsIncluded
bools.comment: the book includes major, minor, and almost-gods (demigods), plus a few divine monsters and magic items

bools.name: dgaMatchForDeitiesAscended
bools.comment: characters who become a match for the deities are to be ranked amongst their number and removed from daily campaign interaction (the ascension seed in the foreword)

bools.name: dgaThreeFourthsSourced
bools.comment: three-fourths of the information was drawn from knowledgeable sources rather than the imagination of the authors (the preface)

bools.name: dgaScaledDown
bools.comment: when a being was made too all-powerful in AD&D terms we scaled them down to be compatible in game terms (the preface)

bools.name: dgaBeginningFramework
bools.comment: the book should be used as a beginning framework for the DM - sample it and take what is wanted (the preface)

bools.name: dgaChaosiumCredit
bools.comment: special thanks are given to Chaosium, Inc. for permission to use the Cthulhu Mythos and the Melnibonean Mythos material (print p. 4, the credits)

bools.name: dgaSecondPrinting
bools.comment: the Chaosium credit is present, the only 1st-vs-2nd printing delta - the upload is the 1980 second printing

bools.name: dgaFreqUnique
bools.comment: unique indicates that there is only one of the creature in existence

bools.name: dgaNumAppearingGuideline
bools.comment: number appearing is furnished as a guideline only, not generally recommended for establishing dungeon level populations

bools.name: dgaAcMagicalNature
bools.comment: a god or hero armor class may not jibe with stated armor and dexterity due to the magical nature of the being

bools.name: dgaMoveTwoMediums
bools.comment: a doubled move number indicates the creature can travel in two mediums or modes (flying, swimming, burrowing, web)

bools.name: dgaInfiniteMoveTeleport
bools.comment: infinite movement is a sort of continuous no-error teleport ability to any point desired

bools.name: dgaDeityHpBanish
bools.comment: hit points killed for a deity means temporarily banished back to its plane of origin, not measure of attack ability

bools.name: dgaMrStandardDoctrine
bools.comment: magic resistance is the percentage chance of a spell absolutely failing, at the 11th level base, adjusted 5% per level either way

bools.name: dgaMrPossessionsOnly
bools.comment: a creature magic resistance extends only to its immediate possessions - anything carried or worn

bools.name: dgaMrAreaEffectNote
bools.comment: area-effect spells will still function if targeted, even against a magic-resistant creature

bools.name: dgaMrSavesStillApply
bools.comment: even if a spell does affect a magic-resistant creature, it is entitled to normal saving throws if applicable

bools.name: dgaClassGridDoctrine
bools.comment: the five-slot class grid: CLERIC/DRUID, FIGHTER, MAGIC-USER/ILLUSIONIST, THIEF/ASSASSIN, MONK/BARD - Nth level X or Nil (the stat block format)

bools.name: dgaHitPointsNotDice
bools.comment: deity stat blocks list hit POINTS, not hit dice (the stat block format finding)

bools.name: dgaWisdomSpellBonusesApply
bools.comment: wisdom spell bonuses apply to the number of spells a divine CLERIC/DRUID can have

bools.name: dgaDruidNeedNotNeutral
bools.comment: a divine being need not be of neutral alignment to have levels of druidical ability

bools.name: dgaMultiClassInconsistent
bools.comment: nothing prevents deities from functioning in several different apparently-inconsistent classes at once

bools.name: dgaMagicLevelFloor
bools.comment: the deity magic-ability level is its highest class level, unless that is less than the 15/20/25 floor by divine rank

bools.name: dgaStrengthParen
bools.comment: the strength score is always followed in parentheses by the being bonus to hit and damage, corresponding to the over-18 table

bools.name: dgaDeityAlignmentLoose
bools.comment: deities are not always constrained to follow their alignment to the letter - their motives and purposes are far above the mortal

bools.name: dgaClericAlignIdentical
bools.comment: the alignment of the deity clerics must be identical with their patron (the explanatory notes)

bools.name: dgaSizeThreeFold
bools.comment: size is abbreviated S (smaller than human), M (man-sized), L (larger than man-sized with greater mass)

bools.name: dgaIntIllusionCumulative
bools.comment: the intelligence illusion/phantasm immunities are cumulative with higher intelligence

bools.name: dgaIntNeverFooled
bools.comment: beings of very high intelligence will not be fooled by illusion/phantasm spells - a 19 intelligence never believes a 1st level illusion

bools.name: dgaWisdomImmunitiesCumulative
bools.comment: the wisdom spell immunities are cumulative with higher wisdom

bools.name: dgaWisdomAutoThrowOff
bools.comment: beings with high wisdom are simply able to automatically throw off the effects of the immune spells

bools.name: dgaDexThiefColsNote
bools.comment: the dexterity thief-skill columns (picking pockets, open locks, traps, move silently, hide) apply only to beings with thief, assassin or monk abilities

bools.name: dgaConRerollDoctrine
bools.comment: the constitution no-1s doctrine: 1s rolled on hit dice count as 2s; at 21-22 the 1s and 2s count as 3s, and so on

bools.name: dgaConNonFighterCap2
bools.comment: beings without fighter, paladin or ranger class receive no more than 2 bonus hit points per die

bools.name: dgaAweDivineOnly
bools.comment: the awe power applies only to divine beings (gods and demigods) - mortals with godlike charisma do not radiate it

bools.name: dgaAweStunNoSave
bools.comment: the awe stun works through any control up to and including a magic jar spell, with no saving throw

bools.name: dgaAweStunnedDefendOnly
bools.comment: creatures stunned by awe can initiate nothing but physical defense if attacked

bools.name: dgaHorrorDivineOnly
bools.comment: the horror aura applies only to the truly ghastly divine beings - a cursed non-divine negative charisma does not confer it

bools.name: dgaHorrorDefendOnly
bools.comment: a horror-stunned creature can do nothing but defend itself physically until the being leaves sight

bools.name: dgaNegativeChaNoHenchmen
bools.comment: beings with negative charisma will never have henchmen of a normal nature

bools.name: dgaPsionicLevelFloor
bools.comment: psionic disciplines function at a minimum level of 15th for demigods, 20th for lesser gods and 25th for greater gods

bools.name: dgaCommandNoSave
bools.comment: the command ability has no saving throw vs. this divine ability

bools.name: dgaComprehendSpeakWrite
bools.comment: the comprehend languages divine ability also grants the ability to speak or write the language in question

bools.name: dgaDetectAlignNoError
bools.comment: the detect alignment ability enables the deity to detect the alignment of objects or creatures with no error

bools.name: dgaGateSameMythos
bools.comment: the deity can only attempt to gate in other beings of the same mythos

bools.name: dgaQuestNoSave
bools.comment: the quest divine ability carries no saving throw

bools.name: dgaTeleportNoError
bools.comment: the teleport ability allows the deity to move from place to place or plane to plane with no error

bools.name: dgaAbilitiesAtWillNotContinuous
bools.comment: the standard abilities all function instantaneously and at will, but not continuously

bools.name: dgaBonusPowersDmJudgment
bools.comment: the gods sometimes manifest surprising abilities - changing ability scores, granting wishes, teleporting others - at DM judgment

bools.name: dgaPowerFromWorshipers
bools.comment: the source of a deity godhead is connected to earthly worshipers; power often increases or decreases as worshiper numbers vary

bools.name: dgaRaisedAbilitiesNoDivine
bools.comment: a human raised into the 20s by ultra-potent magic does not gain the powers reserved for the gods

bools.name: dgaGodsNotMonsterLists
bools.comment: the statistics do not tell how a deity should be played - treating gods as lists of armor classes reduces them to mere monsters

bools.name: dgaFlatterySeenThrough
bools.comment: any god with a wisdom score above 15 knows flattery for what it is and generally guesses the flatterer motives

bools.name: dgaInt20PredictsAction
bools.comment: gods with intelligence above 20 can often tell what action a mortal is about to attempt from preparatory motions

bools.name: dgaAvoidDefeatTeleport
bools.comment: a god in combat always attempts to avoid physical defeat - the innate teleport leaves or blinks away, taking no time or concentration

bools.name: dgaSummonAidDepart
bools.comment: deities in combat almost always summon a retinue, and many gods then depart the field leaving the retinue to fight

bools.name: dgaDeitiesAvoidEachOther
bools.comment: unless they have a history of mutual antipathy, deities are always unwilling to fight other deities, backing off from confrontation

bools.name: dgaGateBringsServants
bools.comment: gate spells are more likely to bring one of the god followers than the deity; a gate spell cannot compel a deity appearance

bools.name: dgaSpecificAidRare
bools.comment: specific aid to individuals is extremely rare; the gods prefer subtle general aid to their worshipers as a whole

bools.name: dgaEvilGodsAppearForConverts
bools.comment: the evil gods, demons and devils are prone to appear when their name is spoken - provided they stand to gain converts

bools.name: dgaInterventionNoWhim
bools.comment: intervention by a deity is no trifling matter and is not to be allowed on a whim, even if characters are in extremis

bools.name: dgaFirstRequestRule
bools.comment: an exemplary character gets the straight 10% creature-sent chance only the first time help is asked

bools.name: dgaDeityComesOn00
bools.comment: if 00 is rolled there is a percentage chance equal to the character level that the deity itself comes, modified by the intervention table

bools.name: dgaCharactersBecomeIntervention
bools.comment: characters asked to take part in the maneuverings of the gods may actually become part of the intervention itself

bools.name: dgaInterventionPrimeOnly
bools.comment: the intervention modifiers apply only to activities on the Prime Material Plane

bools.name: dgaInterventionNoOuterPlanes
bools.comment: deities will not intervene on the planes which are the habitations of other deities, i.e. the Outer Planes

bools.name: dgaInterventionNotPosNeg
bools.comment: deities will neither venture to involve themselves in the Positive or Negative Material Planes

bools.name: dgaInterventionElementalDmOption
bools.comment: intervention in the Elemental Planes is subject to DM option; if there are elemental gods, the Outer Planes deities will NOT go there

bools.name: dgaInterventionOccasionalAstral
bools.comment: intervention occurs only on the Prime Material Plane in most cases, with occasional intervention in the Astral and Ethereal Planes

bools.name: dgaSpells12KnowledgeFaith
bools.comment: 1st and 2nd level cleric spells are gained through the cleric knowledge and faith, not prayer

bools.name: dgaSpells345ServantsMinions
bools.comment: 3rd, 4th and 5th level spells are granted by the supernatural servants or minions of the deity, ranging up to demigod level

bools.name: dgaDemigodDirect345
bools.comment: clerics whose patrons are demigods receive their 3rd through 5th level spells directly from their deity

bools.name: dgaDemigodNo67
bools.comment: a cleric of a demigod could never receive 6th or 7th level spells

bools.name: dgaSixthSeventhFromDeity
bools.comment: sixth and seventh level spells are granted to clerics directly from their deities

bools.name: dgaSeventhGreaterOnly
bools.comment: only the greater gods may grant 7th level spells

bools.name: dgaRankAlterable
bools.comment: the DM may carefully consider altering the demigod/lesser/greater designations if they do not suit the campaign

bools.name: dgaSavesIrreducible
bools.comment: gods and heroes saving throw numbers are irreducible regardless of magical aids and adjustments

bools.name: dgaClericExemplary
bools.comment: clerics are expected to behave in a manner exemplary of the teachings of their faith, role models exhibiting greater wisdom

bools.name: dgaClericRitualsRequired
bools.comment: cleric adventurers must maintain appearances and perform the proper rituals essential to their faith and alignment

bools.name: dgaClericTempleBuilding
bools.comment: clerics build places of worship from roadside shrines to whole temples, in places of relative security - desecration is a terrible blow to a religion honor

bools.name: dgaMinorTransgressionWarningOmen
bools.comment: a minor offense by a higher level cleric typically brings an unmistakable omen sent by one of the deity servants

bools.name: dgaSpellsDeniedDuringAtonement
bools.comment: until the atonement period is complete, use of certain spells or spell levels may be denied the errant cleric

bools.name: dgaGraveSinAllPossessions
bools.comment: a grave transgression may require sacrificing all possessions and going on a major quest to restore good standing

bools.name: dgaExcommunicationTotal
bools.comment: irredeemable sins bring immediate and total excommunication - never again clerical spells in that deity name, nor aid from its followers

bools.name: dgaOmensCorrectionDevices
bools.comment: omens are devices for judges (the DM) to use in correcting players that constantly do improper things

bools.name: dgaOmenPartialPowerLoss
bools.comment: the most common bad omen is a partial loss of power: forgotten higher-level spells, constant illness (one-fourth to one-half hit points), failed renewals

bools.name: dgaOmenEscalation
bools.comment: if a temporary loss of power does not deter the player, more severe omens can be given or the effects made permanent

bools.name: dgaOmenResultsOptional
bools.comment: any and all omen powers or results are entirely optional; a player cannot badger a DM into bonuses for carrying lucky charms

bools.name: dgaOmenGoodPortents
bools.comment: good-luck portents: finding a four-leaf clover, seeing the crescent moon, and finding a toadstool

bools.name: dgaOmenGoodSymbols
bools.comment: good-luck symbols: dice, crossed fingers, a shoe, a fish, a dog, a wheel, and the three apes that see, hear and speak no evil

bools.name: dgaOmenMistletoe
bools.comment: finding mistletoe in the wild is good luck; boiled with pure spring water it is a universal cure for poisons

bools.name: dgaOmenLeatherRepels
bools.comment: the wearing of leather from top to bottom is said to repel demons and devils

bools.name: dgaOmenDung
bools.comment: dung has both properties: the dung-covered cannot be touched by the undead, but dung cast on a good altar defiles it

bools.name: dgaOmenMirrorSalt
bools.comment: breaking a mirror and spilling salt are universally recognized bad omens

bools.name: dgaOmenCelestials
bools.comment: the appearance of meteors, comets and eclipses portends great changes or happenings, usually not good

bools.name: dgaOmenOldWoman
bools.comment: meeting an old woman as one sets out on a journey is ill fortune

bools.name: dgaOmenBatWindow
bools.comment: a bat flying in the window is ill fortune

bools.name: dgaOmenTripping
bools.comment: tripping as one enters a doorway is ill fortune

bools.name: dgaOmenBirdOnSymbol
bools.comment: a bird perched on a holy symbol means horrible things will happen to that sect in the near future

bools.name: dgaOmenCrossedKnives
bools.comment: finding crossed knives in a room is a sure sign that person will be cut the very next time they are attacked

bools.name: dgaOmenThirteen
bools.comment: thirteen of anything in one group is the height of bad luck; taking objects from a group of thirteen invites a horrible death

bools.name: dgaOmenWispFire
bools.comment: the coming of a will-o-wisp means some building is going to burn to the ground within seven days

bools.name: dgaOmenBanshee
bools.comment: the wail of a banshee certainly means someone is going to die that very night

bools.name: dgaOmenRainbow
bools.comment: a rainbow is a definite statement from a deity: either it wants to converse with a mortal or to give the mortal a quest

bools.name: dgaOmenBifrost
bools.comment: in Norse legend men and women of power could travel to Asgard by touching a rainbow (part of the bridge Bifrost) and wishing to be there

bools.name: dgaSoulSpiritDoctrine
bools.comment: the anima is one of two sorts: souls (the five raiseable races) or spirits (all other beings that worship deities, the DM deciding case by case)

bools.name: dgaSpiritMinIntLow
bools.comment: monsters with spirits must have at least an intelligence rating of Low

bools.name: dgaSoulPlaneDmChoice
bools.comment: the plane a soul or spirit goes to is the DM call, judged on the alignment behavior of the mortal life; the faithful pass to their deity plane

bools.name: dgaSoulEternalResident
bools.comment: for souls the destination plane is the beginning of eternity - the soul remains there forever, enjoying the benefits or suffering the torments

bools.name: dgaSpiritRewardsLess
bools.comment: spirits are but temporary residents: their rewards and punishments are less than that received by souls

bools.name: dgaSpiritReincarnation
bools.comment: a spirit can be returned to the Prime Material Plane - reincarnated with no overt memories, the new form not necessarily the same as the old

bools.name: dgaRaisedLimitRationale
bools.comment: the 3-30 day death lag is the rationale for the progressive time limit on the raise dead spell - the farther the soul has travelled, the more powerful the cleric needed

bools.name: dgaAstralPerilDoctrine
bools.comment: the road through the Astral Plane is clearly marked for the dead but not free of peril - hence burial chambers with weapons, treasure and bodyguards

bools.name: dgaResurrectionCooperation
bools.comment: resurrection recalls the soul from its deity plane with that deity cooperation; resurrecting a radically different alignment may greatly offend

bools.name: dgaServantsAreSpirits
bools.comment: the minions of some deities (demons, devils, couatl, ki-rin, titans) are actually spirits put into those forms; the MONSTER MANUAL forms are not the only ones

bools.name: dgaImmortalityEternalYouth
bools.comment: immortality does not confer everlasting existence - what the gods enjoy is eternal youth

bools.name: dgaLongevityPotionReversal
bools.comment: a character with apparent immortality through potions of longevity need not fear natural causes until the final potion reverses all previous ones

bools.name: dgaSilverCordUnbreakable
bools.comment: the silver cord anchoring traveling deities and minions to their home plane cannot be broken by the Psychic Wind or any other means

bools.name: dgaCordPullNearInstant
bools.comment: the cord pulls a spirit back to its plane of origin near-instantaneously when its material form is destroyed, at enormous energy cost

bools.name: dgaDeityDeathFades
bools.comment: when a deity dies on the Prime Material Plane the person and possessions fade away and disappear, though certain items might remain at DM discretion

bools.name: dgaDormancyBlocksSpells
bools.comment: during a resting deity dormancy its clerics can acquire or recover no spells of third level or higher

bools.name: dgaDormancyReadAsOmen
bools.comment: the dormancy spell loss may be interpreted with dismay as a bad omen, but no information will be forthcoming until the dormancy is over

bools.name: dagaDeityNeverAdmitsDefeat
bools.comment: it is unlikely that a deity would admit to its followers that it had been defeated

bools.name: dgaHomePlaneDeathAbsolute
bools.comment: a being slain on its home plane is absolutely and irrevocably dead - no power in the multiverse can restore it, including other deities

bools.name: dgaHomePlaneDeityNearImpossible
bools.comment: it should be next to impossible for anything except another deity to slay a deity on its own plane; brazen characters are dealt with severely

bools.name: dgaAscLevelAboveAverage
bools.comment: the first requirement: an experience level significantly above the average of adventure-type characters in the campaign

bools.name: dgaAscAbilitiesRaised
bools.comment: the second requirement: ability scores raised through mighty world-shaking magic to be on par with the lesser demigods - dozens of wishes, each aging the caster 3 years

bools.name: dgaAscSincereWorshipers
bools.comment: the third requirement: a body of sincere worshipers, genuine and honest in their adoration, convinced by witnessed mighty deeds and miracles

bools.name: dgaAscFaithfulFollower
bools.comment: the fourth requirement: the person must be and have been a faithful and true follower of his or her alignment and patron deity

bools.name: dgaAscDivineQuests
bools.comment: with all four conditions met and a sufficient number of divine quests fulfilled, the deity may invest the person with divine power

bools.name: dgaServantCenturiesToDemigod
bools.comment: the ascended serve as minor functionaries; after several centuries of superior service, exceptional servants may be awarded demigod status with an earthly priesthood

bools.name: dgaAscensionRemovesFromCampaign
bools.comment: ascension to divinity effectively removes the character from the general campaign as a non-player member of the DM pantheon

chains.name: dgaIntRating
chains.comment: the monster intelligence rating ladder (the explanatory notes): band 0 non-intelligent or not ratable, 1 animal, 2 semi-intelligent (2-4), 3 low (5-7), 4 average human (8-10), 5 very intelligent (11-12), 6 highly intelligent (13-14), 7 exceptionally intelligent (15-16), 8 genius (17-18), 9 supra-genius (19-20), and the tail band 10 godlike (21 and above)
